dedupe_keys.name: idb olas population based water stress and risk dataset for latin america and the caribbean 62 798 municipality basin units 27 countries aqueduct 3 0 indicators 2020

description: The Inter-American Development Bank publishes, as part of its Water and Sanitation Observatory for Latin America and the Caribbean (OLAS), a dataset that estimates the population and land area exposed to water stress and water risk in every municipality of 27 countries. Contents: 62,798 rows, each the intersection of a municipality (GADM level 2) with an Aqueduct hydrological unit, carrying the Aqueduct 3.0 categories for baseline water stress, water depletion, interannual and seasonal variability, groundwater decline, riverine and coastal flood risk, drought risk, untreated connected wastewater, coastal eutrophication, unimproved drinking water and sanitation, peak RepRisk and overall water risk, with 2020 WorldPop population and area estimates for each class. Producer: IDB Water and Sanitation Division, method in technical note IDB-TN-2411. Coverage: 27 borrowing and Caribbean countries, reference year 2020. Format and access: CSV (70 MB) from IDB Open Data with a DOI and a CKAN datastore API; no registration. Licence: CC BY 4.0. Caveats: the hazard classes are Aqueduct's global model outputs, not local measurements, and population is modelled, so small municipalities carry large uncertainty. Simulation uses: screening water supply systems and cities for scarcity and flood exposure, prioritising adaptation investment by municipality, and weighting demand scenarios in capacity planning. Related records: the WRI Aqueduct water risk atlas (data-wri-aqueduct-water-risk-atlas) supplies the underlying indicators.
